correctness.rationale: For any width-two poset, two chain decompositions define contiguous allowable gaps for every element of one chain; writing each label at every permissible gap produces a common supersequence of every linear extension of length \(n+i(P)\). Ply-two interval overlap graphs are triangle-free by Helly and chordal by minimum-right-endpoint, hence forests with i(P)=n-c. A path of intervals realizes the identity and every adjacent swap; for a fixed identity embedding the reversed-order embedding of each swapped edge forces an extra earlier right-label occurrence or later left-label occurrence, uniquely chargeable to that edge, proving m-1 extra letters. Add isolated components to cover every (n,c). Direct finite enumeration corroborates but does not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper motivates sorting-supersequences as a canonical preprocessing object and proves only asymptotic size results for general intervals. A complete exact worst-case extremal value \(2n-c\) for every ply-two instance size and component count removes the unknown constant, is sharp even on interval paths, and reveals a useful general two-chain poset construction. The bound is a natural infinite classification and does not depend on a subjective numerical threshold.
